orthonormal real tangent basis $e_i$, write $v=\sum_i v_i e_i$ and
$G=\sum_i df_x(e_i)e_i$. Then
$\langle G,v\rangle=\sum_i df_x(e_i)v_i=df_x(v)$ by linearity, and
if $H$ has the same pairing with every $v$, taking $v=G-H$ gives
$\|G-H\|^2=0$, hence $G=H$. The zero tangent space has $G=0$.
Thus the gradient is well-defined for a $C^2$ objective. First-order
